thread.title: Midday Update: U.S. Stocks Perk Up As US Said to Extend Trade Invitation to China

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: U.S. Stocks Perk Up As US Said to Extend Trade Invitation to China
text:
Shutterstock photo The Dow Jones Industrial Average was jolted higher at mid-morning Tuesday when headlines the U.S. and China would restart trade negotiations catapulted the blue chip index to a two-week high. Led by gains in Boeing ( BA ) and energy names, the Dow traded with a triple-digit gain before retreating from the session high.
According to The Wall Street Journal, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin extended the invitation to Chinese officials before the White House pulls the trigger on another $200 billion in tariffs against Chinse imports. With the help from hurricane-fueled gains in the energy sector and benign inflation data, the Dow raced past 26,000, outpacing gains in the S&P 500.
But while the Dow and S&P gain altitude the Nasdaq continues to languish in negative territory, weighed by downgrades in the semiconductor sector. The tech sector is also taking a hit from a Senate request to executives of Twitter ( TWTR ), Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) and Amazon ( AMZN ) to testify about consumer data privacy issues. The news spooked tech investors who were reminded of last week's Senate appearance by Twitter's Jack Dorsey and Facebook's ( FB ) Sheryl Sandberg that left Facebook and Twitter share prices 5% and 12% lower, respectively.
On the economic front, Wall Street largely ignored an unexpected 0.1% decline in wholesale prices (nominal and core), well below estimates for an increase of 0.2%, and the first decline in the producer price index in 18 months. On an annual basis, the nominal PPI was up 2.8% versus 3.3% previously, while the core was up 2.3% from 2.7% last.
European markets turned higher in concert with the U.S. as easing trade war tensions gave a boost to emerging markets as well. France's CAC-40 lead the pack with a 0.92% gain with the Euro-Stoxx regaining momentum following a miss on EU industrial production.
Crude oil was up $1.14 to $70.39 per barrel. Natural gas was unchanged at $2.83 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $7.70 to $1,210.80 an ounce, while silver was up $0.12 to $14.27 an ounce. Copper was up $0.06 to $2.68 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 1.58% to $14.83 with the United States Natural Gas Fund down 0.11% to $23.18. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 2.23% to 17.96 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.68% to $113.99. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.83% to $13.39.
